competency_fulfillment.rationale: 13 of 17 samples exercise the read/write-notation verbs (e.g. "How is ₱3425 written in words?", "How is 'four thousand four hundred ten pesos' written using the peso symbol?"), but 4 samples (seeds 50, 55, 500, 607) ask pupils to "Use coins and bills to make exactly ₱1286" or count a coin display, producing a plain numeric answer with no words, symbol, PhP, or centavo-sign notation at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All four named notations (words, ₱ symbol, PhP, centavo sign) appear as a correct answer at least once, but the PhP notation surfaces in only 1 of the 17 samples (seed 502, "How is ₱1325 written using the currency code PhP?"), far thinner than the peso symbol's 6 correct occurrences or words' 4.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Phrasing stays single-step and concrete for Grade 3 Quarter 2, e.g. "How is 25 centavos written as a decimal of a peso using the ₱ symbol?", and number-word forms like "four thousand three hundred fourteen pesos" use standard hyphenation without introducing multi-step arithmetic.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four formatters appear (mcq, cloze, read_mcq, set_fill_in_blank) and both write and read directions are tested, but the centavo-sign items use only two distinct values, 25 centavos (seeds 46, 72) and 50 centavos (seeds 603, 606), so contextual variety on that named notation is narrow.

competency_alignment.rationale: 13 of 17 samples vary difficulty through notation type and digit length as this competency requires, but seeds 50, 55, 500 and 607 instead vary difficulty by coin/bill composition, e.g. "Use coins and bills to make exactly ₱9852. Use the fewest pieces possible.", an axis this competency's wording never names.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Whole-peso correct answers span from ₱414 (seed 601) up to ₱9852 (seed 607), staying under the competency's stated ceiling of "up to ₱10 000" while reaching close to it, and no sample's amount exceeds that ceiling.
